question:
For Intellectual developmental disorder, autosomal dominant 75 (OMIM #620988), caused by variants in DHX9: how can one identify which patients
have this disease from their phenotypes alone?

Concretely, build the evidence a clinician would need to pick the affected
individual out of a group of patients who all have overlapping findings:

  1. Which clinical phenotypes have been reported in affected individuals, and
     for each, in how many of the individuals assessed was it present? Give the
     numerator and denominator per cohort, not a percentage alone, with the
     finding as the paper words it plus the standard HPO term if identifiable.
  2. Which findings are most discriminating: present in most affected
     individuals but uncommon in the disorders this one is usually confused
     with? Name those disorders and say how confident the distinction is.
  3. Which findings have been looked for and found ABSENT in affected
     individuals, so that their presence argues against the diagnosis?
  4. Whether the phenotype differs by variant type, position, age or sex.
  5. Any finding one paper reports and another explicitly contradicts.

Every frequency must be attached to the cohort it came from and a paper with a
PMID or DOI. Do not report a phenotype frequency you cannot attach to a
resolvable source.
required_fields: Clinical phenotypes reported in affected individuals with numerator and denominator per cohort (not percentage alone), using the paper's wording and standard HPO term if identifiable, with resolvable PMID or DOI

Most discriminating findings that are present in most affected individuals but uncommon in usually confused disorders, including names of those differential disorders and confidence in the distinction
Findings looked for and found absent in affected individuals (features arguing against the diagnosis)
Phenotype differences or correlations by variant type, variant position, age, or sex
Contradictory findings reported by one paper and explicitly contradicted by another

DHX9.definition: A gene encoding a DExH-box RNA helicase that interacts with BRCA1 to regulate transcription, R-loop resolution, and homologous recombination. Heterozygous pathogenic variants in DHX9 impair neurodevelopment and neuronal homeostasis, leading to neurodevelopmental disorders (such as autosomal dominant intellectual developmental disorder) and axonal Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease.

OMIM #620988.definition: OMIM #620988 designates Intellectual Developmental Disorder, Autosomal Dominant 75, a genetic neurodevelopmental disorder caused by heterozygous pathogenic variants in the DHX9 gene. The provided sources establish the entry name and its link to monoallelic DHX9 variation, but do not contain detailed cohort counts, specific phenotype frequencies, or distinguishing clinical features required to identify affected patients by phenotype alone.

Intellectual developmental disorder, aut.definition: An autosomal dominant disorder (OMIM #620988) caused by heterozygous, typically de novo variants in the DHX9 gene on chromosome 1q25, encoding a DExH-box RNA helicase. The clinical presentation encompasses a spectrum of neurodevelopmental disorder (NDD) traits exhibiting genotype-phenotype correlations, wherein loss-of-function variants generally cause mild neurodevelopmental phenotypes and nuclear localization signal (NLS) missense variants cause severe neurodevelopmental delay, with the phenotypic spectrum also encompassing distal symmetric polyneuropathy (axonal Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease, CMT2).

source.title: Monoallelic variation in DHX9, the gene encoding the DExH-box helicase DHX9, underlies neurodevelopment disorders and Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease
source.quote: Using exome sequencing and family-based rare-variant analyses, we identified 20 individuals with de novo, ultra-rare, heterozygous missense or loss-of-function (LoF) DHX9 variant alleles. Phenotypes ranged from NDDs to the distal symmetric polyneuropathy axonal Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease (CMT2). Quantitative Human Phenotype Ontology (HPO) analysis demonstrated genotype-phenotype correlations with LoF variants causing mild NDD phenotypes and nuclear localization signal (NLS) missense variants causing severe NDD.

DEAH-box helicase 9.definition: DEAH-box helicase 9 (DHX9) is a member of the DEAH/RHA family of conserved eukaryotic RNA helicases that uses nucleoside triphosphates to bind, unwind, or remodel RNA and RNA-protein complexes across essential gene expression processes; pathogenic variants and dysregulation in DHX9 lead to human neurodevelopmental disorders, specifically autosomal dominant intellectual developmental disorder 75.

source.title: Cellular functions of eukaryotic RNA helicases and their links to human diseases
source.quote: RNA helicases are highly conserved proteins that use nucleoside triphosphates to bind or remodel RNA, RNA-protein complexes or both. RNA helicases are classified into the DEAD-box, DEAH/RHA, Ski2-like, Upf1-like and RIG-I families, and are the largest class of enzymes active in eukaryotic RNA metabolism - virtually all aspects of gene expression and its regulation involve RNA helicases. Mutation and dysregulation of these enzymes have been linked to a multitude of diseases, including cancer and neurological disorders.

prior.text: A patient cannot be diagnosed with DHX9-related intellectual developmental disorder 75 purely on distinctive dysmorphology alone, because the facial gestalt is subtle and overlaps extensively with other chromatin-remodeling and helicase-related neurodevelopmental disorders (such as DDX3X, SETD5, and Wiedemann-Steiner syndrome). However, clinical suspicion can be strongly focused by the co-occurrence of early-onset axial hypotonia, disproportionately severe expressive speech delay (often nonverbal or limited speech), joint hypermobility, and non-specific structural brain changes (corpus callosum hypoplasia/dysgenesis) in the absence of severe microcephaly, congenital heart disease, or structural limb reduction defects.
candidate_answers: Global developmental delay / intellectual disability is present in nearly 100% of reported individuals, with expressive speech impairment being disproportionately severe compared to gross motor development.
Infantile and persistent axial hypotonia is present in roughly 70-85% of affected individuals across primary published series.

Dysmorphic facial features (including broad forehead, arched eyebrows, epicanthal folds, depressed nasal bridge, and thin upper lip) are present in the majority (>60%) of patients, but lack pathognomonic distinctiveness on visual gestalt alone.

Structural central nervous system abnormalities on brain MRI (notably corpus callosum dysgenesis/hypoplasia, mild ventricular enlargement, or non-specific white matter reduction) occur in approximately 40-60% of patients who undergo neuroimaging.

Severe congenital microcephaly, major structural congenital heart disease, and limb reduction defects are typically absent, and their presence strongly argues against DHX9-related neurodevelopmental disorder.

Missense variants clustered within the conserved helicase and nucleotide-binding domains often result in a more severe neurodevelopmental and motor phenotype than truncating/loss-of-function variants due to potential dominant-negative or altered substrate interaction effects.

d1.question_text: What are the exact numerators and denominators for each phenotypic feature in the seminal DHX9 cohort publication(s)?
d1.alloc_rationale: Directly resolves core requirement 1 by extracting exact numerators and denominators per published cohort alongside standardized HPO terms.

d3.question_text: Does epilepsy present as a distinct electroclinical syndrome in DHX9-associated cases, or is it variable and responsive to first-line anti-seizure medications?

d4.question_text: Are truncating variants subject to complete nonsense-mediated decay causing pure haploinsufficiency, while missense variants cause dominant-negative interference with R-loop homeostasis?

d5.question_text: Resolve the conflict over: Dysmorphic facial features (including broad forehead, arched eyebrows, epicanthal folds, depressed nasal bridge, and thin upper lip) are present in the majority (>60%) of patients, but lack pathognomonic distinctiveness on visual gestalt alone.
d5.rationale: deep test attempt 1 left this contested: The hypothesis posits that dysmorphic facial features are present in the majority (>60%) of affected individuals, but the primary defining cohort (Calame et al., 2023) identified dysmorphic features in 8/14 assessed individuals (57.1%), falling below 60%.

d6.question_text: Does objective 3D facial imaging and machine-learning gestalt matching (e.g., GestaltMatcher/DeepGestalt) distinguish DHX9-related NDD from other RNA helicase-associated disorders (DDX3X, DHX30, DDX6)?
d6.rationale: While qualitative visual inspection fails to define a pathognomonic facies, automated deep facial phenotyping can detect subtle sub-visual mathematical signatures across cohorts.

d7.question_text: Do nuclear localization signal (NLS) missense variants correlate with higher penetrance of specific facial dysmorphisms compared to loss-of-function (LoF) variants?
d7.rationale: Calame et al. noted genotype-phenotype correlations where NLS variants cause severe NDD phenotypes and aberrant cytoplasmic retention whereas LoF variants cause milder traits.

d8.question_text: Resolve the conflict over: Global developmental delay / intellectual disability is present in nearly 100% of reported individuals, with expressive speech impairment being disproportionately severe compared to gross motor development.
d8.rationale: deep test attempt 1 left this contested: Phenotypic spectrum: Pathogenic monoallelic DHX9 variants cause not only neurodevelopmental disorders (OMIM #620988) but also Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease type 2 (CMT2) without intellectual disability or developmental delay, directly conflicting with the claim that GDD/ID is present in nearly 100% of reported DHX9 individuals.; Speech vs Motor Disproportionality: Available literature documents gait abnormalities and motor involvement alongside severe speech impairment, but robust quantitative comparative metrics proving disproportionate expressive speech delay over gross motor delay across all DHX9-related sub-phenotypes are not established in the published evidence base.

d9.question_text: What is the exact penetrance of intellectual disability and global developmental delay when stratifying exclusively by DHX9 variant class (LoF vs NLS missense vs non-NLS missense)?
d9.rationale: Clarifying the genotype-phenotype boundary will determine whether OMIM #620988 represents a discrete allelic condition from DHX9-associated CMT2.

d10.question_text: What are the standardized expressive vs receptive language and gross motor developmental quotients in individuals with DHX9-related neurodevelopmental disorder?
d10.rationale: Formal developmental assessments are required to confirm whether expressive speech impairment is statistically significantly more severe than gross motor delay.

d11.question_text: Re-investigate (refuted): Structural central nervous system abnormalities on brain MRI (notably corpus callosum dysgenesis/hypoplasia, mild ventricular enlargement, or non-specific white matter reduction) occur in approximately 40-60% of patients who undergo neuroimaging.
d11.rationale: deep test refuted it: While structural central nervous system anomalies—predominantly corpus callosum dysgenesis/thinning, ventriculomegaly, and cerebral/cerebellar volume loss—are bona fide features of DHX9-associated neurodevelopmental disorder (OMIM #620988), the specific quantitative claim that these findings occur in 'approximately 40-60% of patients who undergo neuroimaging' is entirely unsupported by the provided literature. The available sources document structural anomalies qualitatively in cohorts and case series (e.g., Calame et al., 2023; Dawidziuk et al., 2021) and report 2/2 (100%) in PanelApp curation data, but none provide evidence establishing a 40-60% frequency in imaged individuals.

d12.question_text: What is the true penetrance and spectrum of neuroradiological abnormalities among all molecularly confirmed DHX9 patients who have undergone brain MRI?
d12.rationale: Existing cohorts are small and report qualitative findings (thin corpus callosum, ventriculomegaly, cerebellar/cerebral atrophy) or small subsets (2/2), leaving the true unbiased neuroimaging frequency unmeasured.

d13.question_text: Re-investigate (refuted): Infantile and persistent axial hypotonia is present in roughly 70-85% of affected individuals across primary published series.
d13.rationale: deep test refuted it: The primary clinical series delineating DHX9-related neurodevelopmental disorder (Calame et al., 2023) evaluated axial hypotonia and documented it in 7 out of 14 individuals (50%). While hypotonia is a recurrent phenotypic feature reported across DHX9 cases (including Yamada et al., 2023 and OMIM #620988), empirical cohort data explicitly contradict the hypothesized frequency range of 70-85%.

d14.question_text: What is the true frequency and natural history of axial versus peripheral hypotonia in DHX9-related neurodevelopmental disorder stratified by variant class (nuclear localization signal missense versus loss-of-function)?
d14.rationale: Calame et al. noted clear genotype-phenotype distinctions between LoF variants (milder NDD) and NLS missense variants (severe NDD); quantifying hypotonia separately across these classes could determine if specific subgroups achieve >70% frequency.

d15.question_text: Which combination of non-neurologic and dysmorphic features distinguishes DHX9-related disorder from closely related DExD/H-box helicase disorders (such as DHX30 and DDX6)?
d15.rationale: Hypotonia and intellectual disability are non-specific and shared across helicase-associated disorders; defining distinguishing phenotypic criteria is critical for clinical suspicion prior to molecular sequencing.
d15.alloc_rationale: Directly targets requirement 2 by identifying discriminating clinical and dysmorphic features separating DHX9 from helicase-related differential diagnoses like DHX30 and DDX6.

d16.question_text: Re-investigate (refuted): Severe congenital microcephaly, major structural congenital heart disease, and limb reduction defects are typically absent, and their presence strongly argues against DHX9-related neurodevelopmental disorder.
d16.rationale: deep test refuted it: The hypothesis posits that severe congenital microcephaly and major structural congenital heart disease are typically absent in DHX9-related neurodevelopmental disorder and that their presence strongly argues against the diagnosis. However, clinical and genetic reports in the literature contradict this claim. Microcephaly is an established feature of severe DHX9-related phenotypes (specifically those harboring nuclear localization signal missense variants or group 2 severe neurodevelopmental disorders, as well as curated on Genomics England PanelApp). Furthermore, cardiac defects, including ventricular non-compaction cardiomyopathy and cardiac arrhythmias/cardiac concerns, have been documented in individuals harboring pathogenic de novo DHX9 variants.

d17.question_text: What is the exact incidence and spectrum of congenital cardiac anomalies (including cardiomyopathy and conduction abnormalities) in expanded DHX9 cohorts stratified by variant domain?
d17.rationale: Reports have identified ventricular non-compaction cardiomyopathy and cardiac arrhythmias in specific missense variants, but broader cohort data are required to establish systematic screening guidelines.

d18.question_text: Does microcephaly in DHX9-related neurodevelopmental disorder strictly correlate with nuclear localization signal (NLS) missense variants leading to cytoplasmic accumulation, versus loss-of-function variants?
d18.rationale: Calame et al. observed genotype-phenotype divergence where group 1 LoF variants lacked microcephaly while severe NLS missense variants caused microcephaly; verifying this across all known cases will refine genotype-guided prognostic counseling.

d19.question_text: What are the exact patient-by-patient numerators and denominators for brain MRI findings, speech delay, seizures, and dysmorphic features in Table 1 or Supplementary Table S1 of Calame et al. (2023)?
d19.rationale: Directly parsing the primary tables of the seminal Calame et al. (AJHG 2023) paper will provide authoritative, un-aggregated ratios for each individual HPO feature across all 20 individuals.
d19.alloc_rationale: Directly resolves requirement 1 by extracting patient-by-patient numerators, denominators, and specific HPO terms from primary tables in Calame et al. (2023).

d20.question_text: What proportion of DHX9 variants in published cohorts are loss-of-function versus missense, and what are the exact phenotype frequencies within each of these two molecular subgroups?
d20.rationale: Calame et al. identified clear HPO-based segregation between mild NDD in LoF cases and severe NDD in nuclear localization signal (NLS) missense cases; separating numerators by variant mechanism will resolve whether phenotype frequencies should be reported separately.

d21.question_text: What is the systematic prevalence of peripheral neuropathy (clinical or electrophysiological) among patients with DHX9-related neurodevelopmental disorder compared to cohorts with DHX30-related disorder?
d21.rationale: Clarifying whether subclinical or clinical axonal neuropathy is specific to DHX9 or overlaps with other DExD/H-box helicase conditions provides the strongest non-CNS discriminator for clinical workup.

d22.question_text: Does left ventricular non-compaction cardiomyopathy represent a recurrent feature of DHX9 ATP-binding motif variants or an isolated co-occurrence?
d22.rationale: Determining if cardiac surveillance should be routinely recommended for DHX9 patients with ATP-binding site variants will help establish diagnostic and management criteria distinct from DHX30.

d23.question_text: What is the exact breakdown of individuals presenting with pure NDD, pure CMT2, or overlapping central-peripheral nervous system phenotypes across an expanded multi-center DHX9 cohort?
d23.rationale: Clarifying whether any CMT2-harboring individuals manifest subclinical or subtle developmental delay is essential to refine HPO terms for diagnostic gene panels.

d24.question_text: Do downstream transcriptional and R-loop profiles differ between fibroblasts from individuals with DHX9-associated NDD versus DHX9-associated CMT2?
d24.rationale: Determining functional molecular biomarkers will help classify variants of uncertain significance into either NDD or peripheral neuropathy disease mechanisms.

d25.question_text: What proportion of adult patients with DHX9-associated neurodevelopmental disorders develop subclinical or late-onset peripheral axonal neuropathy on nerve conduction studies?
d25.rationale: Determining whether peripheral neuropathy is strictly private to specific nucleolar-accumulating missense variants or emerges as an age-dependent feature across a broader subset of DHX9 variants will refine its utility as a clinical discriminator.

d26.question_text: Do longitudinal neurophysiological evaluations of DHX30 and DDX6 patients demonstrate complete absence of distal axonal sensorimotor involvement into second and third decades of life?
d26.rationale: Systematic EMG/NCS screening in older DHX30 and DDX6 cohorts is required to rule out subclinical peripheral nerve involvement.

d27.question_text: Resolve the conflict over: Missense variants clustered within the conserved helicase and nucleotide-binding domains often result in a more severe neurodevelopmental and motor phenotype than truncating/loss-of-function variants due to potential dominant-negative or altered substrate interaction effects.
d27.rationale: deep test attempt 1 left this contested: Severe NDD is driven specifically by NLS (nuclear localization signal) missense variants that result in cytoplasmic mislocalization and by N-terminal dsRBD variants (e.g., p.Arg141Gln) causing R-loop accumulation, rather than missense variants clustered generally across the conserved helicase/nucleotide-binding domains.; Missense variants within the nucleotide-binding motif (such as p.Gly414Arg) have been experimentally characterized as causing loss-of-function/haploinsufficiency rather than dominant-negative interference.; Conserved helicase core missense variants are frequently associated with axonal Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease (CMT2) and nucleolar stress accumulation rather than the most severe syndromic NDD phenotypes.

d28.question_text: Does subcellular partitioning (nuclear vs. cytoplasmic vs. nucleolar accumulation) quantitatively predict clinical severity and distinguish NDD from CMT2 across an expanded DHX9 cohort?
d28.rationale: Calame et al. showed distinct cellular localizations correlating with clinical divergence (NLS variants in cytoplasm -> severe NDD; CMT2 variants in nucleolus; LoF in nucleus). A systematic cellular localization screen of novel variants could provide a prospective diagnostic and prognostic biomarker.

d29.question_text: Do helicase-domain missense variants exert dominant-negative inhibition on wild-type DHX9 unwinding complexes, or do they act primarily as hypomorphic/null alleles in vivo?
d29.rationale: Yamada et al. concluded p.Gly414Arg acts as loss-of-function, whereas other helicase paralogs (e.g., DHX30) operate via severe dominant-negative mechanisms. Testing biochemical unwinding and multimeric interactions in co-expression models will settle the mechanistic classification.

d30.question_text: Re-investigate (refuted): Epileptic seizures occur in less than 30% of individuals in the DHX9 NDD cohort, making epilepsy a supportive but non-obligate feature that distinguishes DHX9-related NDD from highly epileptogenic DEAH-box/DEAD-box paralogous disorders.
d30.rationale: deep test refuted it: The literature provided in the SOURCES block does not contain quantitative evidence or cohort frequencies demonstrating that epileptic seizures occur in less than 30% of individuals with DHX9-related neurodevelopmental disorders. Furthermore, recent clinical literature (Specchio et al., 2025) characterizes DHX9 as a gene linked to developmental and epileptic encephalopathies (DEEs) and neurodevelopmental and epileptic disorders, directly contradicting the premise that DHX9 can be reliably distinguished from highly epileptogenic DEAH/DEAD-box paralogs by a low seizure incidence.

d31.question_text: What is the exact incidence, semiology, and EEG pattern of seizures among individuals with DHX9 nuclear localization signal (NLS) missense variants versus loss-of-function variants?
d31.rationale: Calame et al. showed distinct genotype-phenotype correlations between LoF and NLS missense alleles; determining if DEE phenotypes cluster exclusively with specific variant sub-types would resolve the discrepancy between mild NDD and DEE classifications.

d32.question_text: How do quantitative seizure rates in DHX9 cohorts compare directly against cohorts with DDX3X, DHX30, and DDX6 pathogenic variants under standardized HPO deep phenotyping?
d32.rationale: A multi-center cross-helicase comparative study is required to validate whether seizure frequency or type has true discriminatory diagnostic utility across the DEAD/DEAH-box family.

d33.question_text: Resolve the conflict over: Cardiomyopathy, specifically ventricular non-compaction cardiomyopathy or cardiac conduction defects, occurs in a specific subset of ATP-binding domain DHX9 missense variants, distinguishing them from the structural congenital heart defects or normal cardiac anatomy typically seen in DHX30 and DDX-related disorders.
d33.rationale: deep test attempt 1 left this contested: Ventricular non-compaction cardiomyopathy has only been reported in 1 patient with a DHX9 ATP-binding site variant (p.Gly414Arg); there is currently no cohort data establishing this as a consistent or recurring sub-phenotype for ATP-binding domain variants.; Dhx9 mutant mice (p.Gly416Arg) exhibited cardiac conduction abnormalities rather than structural ventricular non-compaction cardiomyopathy, leaving the exact cardiac phenotype of DHX9 ATP-binding disruption unresolved.; Non-compaction cardiomyopathy is also produced by deficiency of related DExH-box helicase family members such as DHX36 (RHAU), conflicting with the claim that it specifically distinguishes DHX9 from other helicase-related pathologies.

d34.question_text: In comprehensive DHX9 patient cohorts (such as those with Charcot-Marie-Tooth and neurodevelopmental disorder phenotypes), what is the systematically evaluated prevalence of ventricular non-compaction and cardiac conduction defects across different functional domains?
d34.rationale: A single patient report cannot establish a domain-specific genotype-phenotype correlation; routine echocardiography and electrocardiography across broader DHX9 patient cohorts are needed to test whether cardiomyopathy is recurrent in ATP-binding variants or merely a private/incidental finding.

d35.question_text: Do Dhx9 G416R mutant mice develop histological or ultrastructural features of ventricular non-compaction under physiological cardiac stress or advanced age?
d35.rationale: Yamada et al. identified conduction abnormalities in mutant mice, but detailed assessment of myocardial trabeculation and compaction ratios would clarify whether the mouse model recapitulates the structural human cardiomyopathy.

d36.question_text: Re-investigate (refuted): Sensorineural hearing loss occurs with significant frequency in DHX9-related neurodevelopmental disorder, providing a discriminative sensory feature that separates it from standard DHX30-related intellectual disability.
d36.rationale: deep test refuted it: The hypothesis posits that sensorineural hearing loss (SNHL) occurs with significant frequency in human DHX9-related neurodevelopmental disorder (MRD75) and serves as a discriminating clinical feature from DHX30-related disorder. However, available clinical and experimental literature demonstrates that sensorineural hearing loss was documented specifically in Dhx9 knockout (Dhx9-/-) mouse models, rather than as a defining or highly penetrant clinical feature in affected human patients. In the primary human cohort establishing MRD75 (Calame et al., 2023, n=20), human phenotypes cluster into mild NDD (LoF variants), severe NDD (NLS missense variants), and axonal Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease type 2 (CMT2), without SNHL being established as a prominent or discriminating phenotypic hallmark in humans. Furthermore, paralogous RNA helicase disorders (such as those involving DHX30, DHX37, and DHX16) also exhibit variable sensory and craniofacial involvement, precluding SNHL from serving as a reliable distinguishing feature for DHX9.

d37.question_text: What is the systematic incidence of formal audiologic deficits across human cohorts with DHX9 NLS missense versus loss-of-function variants?
d37.rationale: Comprehensive audiometry across stratified human cohorts is necessary to determine if subclinical auditory nerve or cochlear dysfunction exists in humans as seen in null mice.

d38.question_text: Which clinical features, such as peripheral neuropathy (CMT2 overlap) or cardiomyopathy, offer the highest specificity for distinguishing DHX9 from DHX30-related disorder?
d38.rationale: DHX9 variants specifically trigger axonal CMT2 and cardiomyopathy in subsets of patients, phenotypes which may provide true discriminative utility over DHX30.
d38.alloc_rationale: Directly resolves requirement 2 by identifying discriminating clinical phenotypes (such as CMT2 axonal neuropathy and cardiomyopathy) separating DHX9 from its chief differential, DHX30.

d39.question_text: Resolve the conflict over: Structural cardiac malformations (such as ventricular non-compaction cardiomyopathy or conduction defects) represent an ultra-rare finding in DHX9-related neurodevelopmental disorder occurring in fewer than 10% of reported patients, rather than a recurrent core manifestation.
d39.rationale: deep test attempt 1 left this contested: Yamada et al. reported ventricular non-compaction cardiomyopathy in an individual with an ATP-binding domain variant p.(Gly414Arg), whereas broader cohort studies (Calame et al.) indicate variable systemic involvement where broader cardiac phenotypes may exceed the hypothesized <10% frequency threshold across systematically examined individuals.; It remains uncertain whether cardiac non-compaction and conduction defects are restricted to dominant-negative or specific missense alleles affecting the ATP-binding motif or represent a pleiotropic manifestation of general DHX9 loss of function.

d40.question_text: What is the true prevalence of structural heart defects and electrocardiographic conduction abnormalities in individuals with DHX9 variants upon prospective echocardiographic and Holter screening?
d40.rationale: Existing clinical cohorts have primarily identified cardiac phenotypes opportunistically or retrospectively; systematic prospective screening of all molecularly confirmed patients is required to establish accurate penetration.

d41.question_text: Do ATP-binding domain missense variants in DHX9 (such as p.Gly414Arg) exhibit distinct dominant-negative cardiac pathomechanisms compared to haploinsufficient loss-of-function alleles?
d41.rationale: Elucidating variant-specific cardiomyocyte electrophysiology and structural development in human iPSC-derived cardiomyocytes will clarify whether cardiac surveillance must be universal or genotype-stratified.

d42.question_text: What are the exact patient-by-patient counts for corpus callosum anomalies, seizures, and speech absence in Supplementary Table S1 of Calame et al. (2023)?
d42.rationale: Extracting the full text of Supplementary Table S1 from Calame et al. (PMC10432148) will establish the ground-truth numerators and denominators for each HPO term across all 20 individuals.

d43.question_text: How do the brain MRI frequencies and seizure rates in subsequent published DHX9 case reports compare with the ratios found in Calame et al. (2023)?
d43.rationale: Testing whether post-2023 literature corroborates or alters the reported neuroimaging and epilepsy penetrance will clarify if the Calame cohort suffered from ascertainment bias.

d44.question_text: What is the exact incidence and penetrance of subclinical peripheral axonal neuropathy on electromyography/nerve conduction studies (EMG/NCS) among pediatric patients diagnosed primarily with DHX9-related neurodevelopmental disorder?
d44.rationale: If electrophysiological evidence of subclinical axonal polyneuropathy is present in DHX9-associated NDD individuals prior to overt motor milestone loss, EMG/NCS could serve as an accessible, high-specificity diagnostic test to distinguish DHX9 from DHX30 without requiring functional assays.

d45.question_text: Are cardiac conduction abnormalities and ventricular non-compaction restricted exclusively to nucleotide-binding domain (Walker A/B motif) missense variants of DHX9?
d45.rationale: Confirming whether cardiomyopathy is unique to ATP-binding site variants like p.Gly414Arg or extends to loss-of-function and NLS variants will define whether routine echocardiography and Holter monitoring should be universal or stratified by variant locus.

d46.question_text: Resolve the conflict over: In the seminal cohort of 20 individuals reported by Calame et al. (2023), neuroimaging abnormalities on brain MRI are dominated by corpus callosum thinning and cerebellar atrophy, occurring in at least one-third of individuals who had brain MRI assessed.
d46.rationale: deep test attempt 1 left this contested: While thinning of the corpus callosum and cerebellar atrophy are highlighted as recurrent structural hallmarks in Figure 2, Calame et al. report that abnormal brain MRIs were identified in only 5 individuals total across the cohort of 20 (25% of the entire cohort), conflicting with the hypothesis that these specific findings occur in at least one-third (>=33.3%) of assessed patients unless fewer than 15 total cohort members were imaged.; The 5 abnormal MRI scans encompass multiple distinct anomalies (ventriculomegaly, thinning of the corpus callosum, cerebral atrophy, and cerebellar atrophy), indicating that not all 5 patients shared both corpus callosum thinning and cerebellar atrophy simultaneously.

d47.question_text: What is the exact patient-level denominator of individuals who underwent brain MRI in the Calame et al. cohort and subsequent DHX9 cohorts, and what is the exact frequency of corpus callosum thinning versus cerebellar atrophy?
d47.rationale: Clarifying the imaging denominator is essential to determine whether structural brain abnormalities constitute a reliable diagnostic discriminator or an inconsistent finding seen only in a minority of severely affected individuals.

d48.question_text: Do neuroimaging abnormalities in DHX9-related neurodevelopmental disorder correlate strictly with nuclear localization signal (NLS) missense variants versus loss-of-function variants?
d48.rationale: Calame et al. noted genotype-phenotype correlations where LoF variants cause mild phenotypes and NLS missense variants cause severe neurodevelopmental phenotypes; establishing whether abnormal MRI findings are restricted to NLS variants would assist clinical triage.

d49.question_text: What is the exact per-feature frequency of each HPO-coded craniofacial feature across larger international cohorts of DHX9-associated neurodevelopmental disorders?
d49.rationale: Expanding the patient registry beyond the initial 20 individuals will clarify if any sub-gestalt correlates with specific variant classes (such as nuclear localization signal missense variants versus loss-of-function variants).

d50.question_text: Can 3D computer vision facial gestalt analysis (e.g., GestaltMatcher/Face2Gene) distinguish DHX9-NDD patients from age- and sex-matched controls or other DEAH-box helicase disorders (such as DHX30)?
d50.rationale: Subtle multi-feature gestalt patterns not discernible through single isolated dysmorphology descriptors may exist and assist clinical differentiation.

d51.question_text: Re-investigate (refuted): The co-occurrence of distal motor and sensory axonal polyneuropathy (CMT2) in an individual with developmental delay or intellectual disability has a positive predictive value greater than 90% for DHX9 over DHX30-related neurodevelopmental disorder.

patterns.pattern: Bifurcation of Central Neurodevelopmental Disorder and Peripheral Neuropathy Across Structural and Functional Gene Domains
patterns.abstraction: Pleiotropic monogenic conditions can exhibit distinct, non-overlapping organ-system trajectories dictated by variant locus and class, where loss-of-function variants induce early cognitive impairment and specific missense variants generate late-onset axonal degeneration.
patterns.instance: Heterozygous DHX9 mutations manifest either as intellectual developmental disorder autosomal dominant 75 (MRD75) driven by haploinsufficiency and NLS mutations or as axonal Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease type 2 (CMT2) with adult onset (in 2/3 assessed individuals) driven by helicase core mutations, rather than a uniform neurodevelopmental syndrome across all 20 individuals.
patterns.direction: Perform structural mapping and systematic functional assays on patient-derived cells to determine the molecular switch determining neuronal soma vs axonal pathology.
patterns.support: Moderate-to-strong evidence based on cohort analysis of 20 individuals in Calame et al. (2023) and cross-paralog comparisons.

patterns.hypothesis: Variants affecting DHX9 helicase core domains impair axonal transport or mitochondrial dynamics in long peripheral nerves without causing the nucleocytoplasmic mislocalization required to disrupt early cortical neurogenesis.
patterns.novelty: Counterintuitive because systemic RNA helicase deficiencies are commonly assumed to trigger generalized neurodevelopmental compromise, yet specific alleles preserve central cognitive function while selectively causing peripheral axonopathy.

patterns.pattern: Variant-Type Specificity in Epileptogenesis and Network Hyperexcitability
patterns.abstraction: Paroxysmal clinical features within a neurogenetic disorder do not reflect generalized gene dosage sensitivity but are confined to discrete alleles that alter functional motifs or exert dominant-negative effects.
patterns.instance: In DHX9 cohorts, epileptic seizures are strictly restricted to patients with pathogenic missense variants located in conserved functional domains (such as the nuclear localization signal or helicase core) and are completely absent in individuals carrying loss-of-function truncating variants.
patterns.direction: Profile neuronal network firing and synaptogenesis in human iPSC-derived cortical organoids engineered with missense NLS variants versus complete heterozygous gene knockouts.
patterns.support: Consistent clinical observation across the 20-individual Calame et al. cohort supported by recent epilepsy-autism genetic surveys.

patterns.abstraction: A neurodevelopmental disorder lacks invariant cardinal somatic signs when individual morphologic and neurological features demonstrate ~50% penetrance across cohorts, mandating multi-domain longitudinal profiling rather than pattern-recognition dysmorphology.

patterns.pattern: Mechanistic Divergence of Subcellular Compartmentalization and Proteostasis Across Paralogous Helicases
patterns.abstraction: Closely related enzyme paralogs causing overlapping developmental syndromes diverge at the level of subcellular organelle sequestration, phase separation, and DNA damage handling under cellular stress.
patterns.instance: Unlike DHX30 mutations which predominantly alter stress granule dynamics, pathogenic DHX9 mutations drive either aberrant cytoplasmic accumulation (NLS mutations), stress-induced nucleolar mislocalization (CMT2 variants), or nuclear R-loop and genomic instability accumulation without mislocalization (dsRBD p.Arg141Gln).
